<script>
  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
    // Pre-apply spinout-banner dismissal here, before the banner paints, so it
    // never flashes in only to be hidden later by the deferred arxiv-header.js.
    // Key matches arxiv-header.js: "arxiv-banner-dismissed:" + data-banner-name.
    if (localStorage.getItem('arxiv-banner-dismissed:spinout-nonprofit')) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-banner-dismissed", "");
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

<article class="ltx_document ltx_authors_1line ltx_leqno">
<h1 class="ltx_title ltx_title_document">Debug2Fix: Supercharging Coding Agents with Interactive Debugging Capabilities</h1>
<div class="ltx_authors">
<span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Spandan Garg
</span><span class="ltx_author_notes"><span class="ltx_author_notes_content">
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_note"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Note: </span>Corresponding author.
</span>
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_email"><span class="ltx_contact_name">email: </span><a href="mailto:spgarg@microsoft.com">spgarg@microsoft.com</a>
</span>
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Affiliation: </span><span id="id1" class="ltx_text ltx_affiliation_institution">Microsoft</span>, <span id="id2" class="ltx_text ltx_affiliation_country">USA</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span class="ltx_author_before"> and </span><span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Yufan Huang
</span><span class="ltx_author_notes"><span class="ltx_author_notes_content">
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_email"><span class="ltx_contact_name">email: </span><a href="mailto:yufanhuang@microsoft.com">yufanhuang@microsoft.com</a>
</span>
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Affiliation: </span><span id="id3" class="ltx_text ltx_affiliation_institution">Microsoft</span>, <span id="id4" class="ltx_text ltx_affiliation_country">USA</span>
</span></span></span></span></div>

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract.</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">While significant progress has been made in automating various aspects of software development through coding agents, there is still significant room for improvement in their bug fixing capabilities. Debugging and investigation of runtime behavior remains largely a manual, developer-driven process. Popular coding agents typically rely on either static analysis of the code or iterative test-fix cycles, which is akin to trial and error debugging. We believe that there is a wealth of rich runtime information that developers routinely access while debugging code, which agents are currently deprived of due to design limitations. Despite how prevalent debuggers are in modern IDEs and command-line tools, they have surprisingly not made their way into coding agents. In this work, we introduce Debug2Fix, a novel framework that incorporates interactive debugging as a core component of a software engineering agent via a subagent architecture. We incorporate debuggers for Java and Python into our agent framework and evaluate against GitBug-Java and SWE-Bench-Live and achieve <math id="abstract1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&gt;" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>&gt;</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&gt;</annotation></semantics></math>20% improvement in performance compared to the baseline for certain models. Furthermore, using our framework, we’re able to make weaker models like GPT-5 and Claude Haiku 4.5 match or exceed the performances of stronger models like Claude Sonnet 4.5, showing that better tool design is often just as important as switching to a more expensive model. Finally, we conduct systematic ablations demonstrating the importance of both the subagent architecture and debugger integration.</p>
  
</div>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1. </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Coding agents <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">1</a>, <a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">2</a>, <a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">3</a>)</cite> demonstrate impressive capabilities in a variety of software engineering tasks. Bug-fixing is among the most common tasks developers perform with agents <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">4</a>)</cite>, yet there remains significant room for improvement <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">5</a>, <a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>, <a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">7</a>)</cite>. Taking a closer look at how agents approach bugs sheds some light on some of the limitations in their bug-fixing capabilities. When faced with bugs or failing tests, coding agents follow one of two strategies: making changes based on pure static code analysis, or entering extended print-debugging sessions, both of which requires the agent to guess the underlying state of the program during execution. In the latter, the agent cycles between examining the program output i.e. reading error messages, stack traces, console logs, etc. to guess the underlying behavior and then making changes based on its interpretation of the output. If the error persists, the agent continues to iterate through the debug and fix steps until the error goes away or it gives up. While this approach works for simpler bugs, the cycle of print-debugging and fixing is not only slow because it depends on repeatedly executing the program with small incremental changes that slowly approach the correct fix, but also unreliable as the agent is guessing runtime behavior rather than observing it directly. Without having access to the actual program state, the agent may make its decisions based on faulty hypotheses and make incorrect changes, which can even seep through human-written test suites <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We argue that this kind of print-debugging that agents primarily rely on, forms a major inefficiency in the debugging capabilities of today’s agents. In contrast to this, expert human developers have long relied on debuggers to diagnose bugs effectively. Debuggers allow developers to pause the program at user-specified locations known as breakpoints, and inspect the values of variables, evaluate arbitrary expressions of code, examine the ongoing call-stack and step through code line by line. This is significantly more precise than inferring program behavior based on simply reading code or print output, where one wrong guess can compound and derail a whole debug session. Furthermore, this is also more efficient because converging on the right set of breakpoints requires fewer iterations than incrementally building an understanding of code based on print outputs alone.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Despite the prevalence of debuggers in modern IDEs and command-line (CLI) tools, they have surprisingly not made their way into coding agents. This is likely due to the fact that debuggers were designed with human-interaction in mind. They require careful orchestration of commands to interact with the program state. Command-line debugger commands are verbose by design as they’re designed to provide as much diagnostic information as possible. Finally, debuggers involve asynchronous events and timing, which is not easy for an agent to manage programmatically. As a consequence, naively exposing a debugger to the agent can lead to brittle interactions and failures. Due to these limitations, an effective schema for debuggers is a non-trivial task. However, it’s also possible that one might go through the exercise of creating a perfect suite of tools only for the agent to never use it <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>)</cite>. In our experiments, providing debug tools directly to the main agent resulted in minimal usage. Despite all these difficulties, we believe that agents not leveraging debuggers represents a significant missed opportunity.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S1.F1" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18571v1/figures/swedebug_2.png" id="S1.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/281;" width="476" height="281" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S1.F1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 1</span>. </span><span id="S1.F1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">A high-level view of the overall Debug2Fix pipeline with the Debug Subagent. We can see that the main agent’s is to loop between querying the Debug Subagent, followed by making fixes based on the learned insights from runtime behavior. Internally, the Debug Subagent works by going through a cycle of setting breakpoints, stepping through code and inspecting variables / expressions until it has the answer to main agent’s query or runs out of turns.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">To address all these gaps we introduce <span id="S1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Debug2Fix</span>, the first specialized agent framework that incorporates debugging as a core component of the agent framework. It works by incorporating debuggers into coding agents via a novel tool design and crucially, a subagent architecture. Rather than exposing the debugger tools to the main agent directly, where they most likely go unused, we expose a unified Debug Subagent to the main agent, which is strongly instructed to use it.
This subagent design encapsulates all the complexities associated with debuggers behind a simple high-level interface for the main agent to use. During inference, the agent offloads debugging tasks to the subagent, which then handles the debugger orchestration via its set of tools and returns a concise answer with all the findings. Our contributions in this work are as follows:</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<ul id="S1.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Debug2Fix</span>: We present the first integration of interactive debugging into a coding agent via the use of a subagent and a novel tool schema, enabling complex runtime debugging capabilities that complement static code analysis. Through our qualitative analysis, we show that the Debug Subagent follows similar workflows as an expert human developer.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Empirical Evaluation &amp; Ablation Study</span>: We conduct an extensive evaluation of our approach by incorporating the Java Debugger (JDB) and Python Debugger (PDB) into a coding agent and evaluate on bug fixing benchmarks like GitBug-Java <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">10</a>)</cite> and SWE-Bench-Live <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>)</cite>. We show that adopting Debug2Fix framework improves performance over vanilla agent by <math id="S1.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&gt;" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>&gt;</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&gt;</annotation></semantics></math>20% relative to baseline numbers in some cases. We also conduct ablation experiments showing that both our tool design and subagent architecture are essential.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2. </span>Background and Related Work</h2>

<div id="S2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We build upon a rich foundation of research in Software Engineering and Agentic AI. Our work bridges a crucial gap in Software Engineering Agents and the typical developer workflow for fixing bugs.</p>
</div>
<section id="S2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.1. </span>Automated Debugging</h3>

<div id="S2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Debugging is a core skill in software development. However it remains largely a manual and human-driven process. There have been works that try to automate debugging. AutoSD <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">12</a>)</cite> prompts LLMs to automatically generate hypotheses and uses debuggers to interact with buggy code. ChatDBG <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">13</a>)</cite> augments traditional debuggers into an AI-powered debugging assistant. While still a human-driven process, it integrates LLMs into debuggers to enhance the user-friendliness of conventional debuggers and allowing humans to have a dialogue with the debugger and pose complex questions. Zhong et al. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">14</a>)</cite> propose an LLM Debugger (LDB) that allows LLMs to refine their own generated programs with runtime information. It segments programs into blocks and tracks intermediate values after each block.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">While these approaches demonstrate the value of runtime information and various forms of debugging, they differ from our work in key ways. Our work is specifically designed to introduce debuggers into automated coding agents that work on the entire repository. It encapsulates debugger complexity behind a high-level interface so that agents can utilize it effectively.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.2. </span>Software Engineering Agents</h3>

<div id="S2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">There have been significant advancements in the field of SE Agents. Starting with SWE-Agent <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">15</a>)</cite>, which proposed key design principles that demonstrated high-performance on repository-level tasks. Since then agent systems like OpenHands <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">3</a>)</cite>, Claude Code <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">1</a>)</cite>, Copilot CLI <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">16</a>)</cite>, VSCode Agent <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">2</a>)</cite>, Windsurf <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">17</a>)</cite> have seen widespread adoption into the developer workflow and demonstrate impressive performance on various software engineering tasks such as test generation, bug fixing, code search, etc.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">While existing agent frameworks have shown impressive capabilities on various benchmarks, gaps still remain when it comes to harder bug-fixing tasks. These agents leverage suboptimal techniques like iterative print-debugging cycles by inserting logging statements into code or making educated guesses based on static analysis of code. Our work addresses these core limitations with agents by incorporating interactive debugging into coding agents as a dedicated subagent.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.3. </span>Multi-Agent Architectures</h3>

<div id="S2.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The use of specialized agents has proven to be an effective pattern in AI Agent Systems. Rather than expecting a single agent / model to have all capabilities, multi-agent systems decompose the high-level problem and delegate responsibilities to smaller agents or subagents. Many works have improved problem-solving abilities of LLMs by integrating discussions among multiple agents. In their survey <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">18</a>)</cite>, He et al. systematically reviewed the landscape of LLM-based multi-agent systems for software engineering highlighting the current capabilities and limitations of these approaches. MASAI <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">19</a>)</cite> proposes a modular architecture for software engineering agents where subagents are instantiated with well-defined objectives and strategies, achieving competitive performance on coding benchmarks. AutoDev <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">20</a>)</cite> uses multiple autonomous AI Agents to achieve user defined objectives. MapCoder <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">21</a>)</cite> is another such framework that consists of several LLM agents, which is designed to simulate the stages of the developer cycle.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Our Debug Subagent follows a modular multi-agent pattern, providing the main agent with a high-level interface for debugging queries while encapsulating the complexity of low-level debugger interactions. Unlike prior works that decompose tasks into code search, localization, repair phases, we introduce a specialized capability that complements static analysis. Through ablation experiments, we show that this architectural choice is essential i.e. when debugging tools are exposed to the main agent directly, they go largely unused. The subagent design is pivotal in making this otherwise low-level capability into a simple interface the main agent readily utilizes.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S2.F2" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">

ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;">start_datetime</span><span id="lstnumberx4.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;">:</span><span id="lstnumberx4.11" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx4.12" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_keyword ltx_lst_keywords2 ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;">int</span><span id="lstnumberx4.13" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;">,</span><span id="lstnumberx4.14" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx4.15" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;">end_datetime</span><span id="lstnumberx4.16" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;">:</span><span id="lstnumberx4.17" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx4.18" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_keyword ltx_lst_keywords2 ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;">int</span><span id="lstnumberx4.19" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;">)</span><span id="lstnumberx4.20" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx4.21" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;">-&gt;</span><span id="lstnumberx4.22" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx4.23" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_keyword ltx_lst_keywords2 ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;">float</span><span id="lstnumberx4.24" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;">:</span>
</span>
<span id="lstnumberx5" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;">        </span><span id="lstnumberx5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_keyword ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;">if</span><span id="lstnumberx5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx5.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;">start_datetime</span><span id="lstnumberx5.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx5.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;">&gt;</span><span id="lstnumberx5.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx5.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;">end_datetime</span><span id="lstnumberx5.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;">:</span>
</span>
<span id="lstnumberx6" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;">&gt;</span><span id="lstnumberx6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;">           </span><span id="lstnumberx6.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_keyword ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;">raise</span><span id="lstnumberx6.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx6.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;">ValueError</span><span id="lstnumberx6.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;">(</span><span id="lstnumberx6.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_string ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;--ltx-fg-color:#FF0000;">"empty<span id="lstnumberx6.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>range<span id="lstnumberx6.7.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>for<span id="lstnumberx6.7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>_rand_seconds:<span id="lstnumberx6.7.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>..."</span><span id="lstnumberx6.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;">)</span>
</span>
<span id="lstnumberx7" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;">E</span><span id="lstnumberx7.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;">           </span><span id="lstnumberx7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;">ValueError</span><span id="lstnumberx7.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;">:</span><span id="lstnumberx7.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx7.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;">empty</span><span id="lstnumberx7.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx7.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_keyword ltx_lst_keywords2 ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;">range</span><span id="lstnumberx7.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx7.10" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_keyword ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;">for</span><span id="lstnumberx7.11" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx7.12" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;">_rand_seconds</span><span id="lstnumberx7.13" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;">:</span>
</span>
<span id="lstnumberx8" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;">E</span><span id="lstnumberx8.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;">             </span><span id="lstnumberx8.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;">start</span><span id="lstnumberx8.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx8.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;">datetime</span><span id="lstnumberx8.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx8.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;">must</span><span id="lstnumberx8.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx8.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;">be</span><span id="lstnumberx8.10" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx8.11" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;">before</span><span id="lstnumberx8.12" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx8.13" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;">than</span><span id="lstnumberx8.14" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx8.15" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;">end</span><span id="lstnumberx8.16" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;"> </span><span id="lstnumberx8.17" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:50%;">datetime</span>
</span>
</span>
<span id="S2.F2.p1.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.F2.p1.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">Not sure if my code is wrong or something, but all was working fine before.</span></span>
</span>
<span id="S2.F2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<span id="S2.F2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.F2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">This is what is failing I think:
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S2.F2.p2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">deadline = factory.Faker("date_time", end_datetime="-1w", tzinfo=timezone.get_current_timezone())</span></span></span>
</span></span>
</div></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">
<div id="S2.F2.4" class="ltx_block ltx_figure_panel ltx_minipage ltx_align_center ltx_align_top" style="width:338.1pt;"><img src="2602.18571v1/figures/traj.png" id="S2.F2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:373/81;" width="373" height="81" alt="Refer to caption">
</div></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S2.F2.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 2</span>. </span><span id="S2.F2.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">A bug from a popular open-source Python repository on GitHub. We see very different trajectories taken by the Baseline Agent and Debug2Fix. In the baseline, we see the agent doing repeated print-debug cycles and arriving at the wrong fix due to not being able to find the root cause of the issue, which is situated deep within the repo. With Debug2Fix, the agent uses the Debug Subagent which is able to find the root cause immediately using a debugger. This results in the agent arriving at the correct fix.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3. </span>Motivating Example</h2>

<div id="S3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we provide an overview of Debug2Fix with a motivating example. Figure <a href="#S2.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 2.3. Multi-Agent Architectures ‣ 2. Background and Related Work ‣ Debug2Fix: Supercharging Coding Agents with Interactive Debugging Capabilities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> shows an example of a bug from a popular open-source python library where the user is trying to generate a random Unix timestamp from up to a week ago (<span id="S3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">-1w</span> in code). The library method works by parsing the <span id="S3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">end_datetime</span> string into a timestamp by computing a time delta of negative seven days compared to the output of the <span id="S3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">_safe_now()</span> method, which is supposed to return the current timestamp. However, buried deep in the class hierarchy, its fallback is set to <span id="S3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">datetime(1970, 1, 1)</span> in one of the code paths. Since this is ‘Unix Time <span id="S3.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">0</span>’, taking a negative timestamp from it results in a crash.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We compare the trajectories of both the baseline agent and our Debug2Fix agent when tasked with solving this problem given the corresponding repo. Looking at the high-level agent trajectories in the figure, we can see that the baseline agent engages in repeated edit and bash calls to do print-debugging, until it believes issue is fixed. Due to how deep in the codebase the issue is, the agent ends up having to do a lot of print debugging as it struggles to find where the bug is coming from. In this case, it actually ends up re-writing the unit test associated with this problem and submitting the wrong fix. Debug2Fix solves this problem with relative ease. Rather than guessing at the program’s runtime behavior through print statements, Debug2Fix delegates the problem of finding the root cause to the Debug Subagent as seen in the figure. The subagent sets a breakpoint directly in the test script and inspects the local variables, while stepping through the code. Looking at the return value of <span id="S3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">_safe_now()</span>, which returns <span id="S3.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">datetime(1970, 1, 1)</span> instead of the current time immediately reveals the root cause of the issue.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">This set of contrasting trajectories was one of many observed across our benchmark evaluations.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4. </span>Methodology</h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we explain the approach behind Debug2Fix in detail and how we incorporate it into an existing coding agent. Figure <a href="#S1.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ 1. Introduction ‣ Debug2Fix: Supercharging Coding Agents with Interactive Debugging Capabilities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> shows a high-level view of the overall approach. We first describe the schema and underlying architecture of the Debug Subagent. Let’s begin by describing what a subagent is:</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Subagent</span>: A subagent is a secondary LLM-based agent that is invoked by the primary (or "main") agent to handle a specialized sub-task. Unlike the main agent, which is meant to solve a broad set of tasks, the subagent solves a smaller, often simpler, set of tasks using a specialized list of tools. Just like the main agent, the subagent has its own system prompt, context window and tool-set that it uses to achieve the goal delegated to it by the main agent.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1. </span>Debug Subagent</h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The Debug Subagent is one such specialized subagent designed to answer questions about runtime behavior. In our case, it’s exposed to the main agent as a simple tool, which can be invoked with the following set of parameters and arguments:</p>
<ul id="S4.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S4.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Runtime Question</span> (Required): The main agent describes what it wants to know about the program’s runtime behavior. This is the only required field.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Test(s)</span> (Required): The main agent provides a script / test that fails.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Path</span> (Optional): This is a path to the code the main agent wants the subagent to exercise.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lines</span> (Optional): These are the lines we want to set the initial breakpoints on.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I1.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Variable</span> (Optional): These are the variables the main agent has told us to pay particular attention to.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">As it’s output, the Debug Subagent returns a structured response containing a final answer to the question asked by the main agent and supporting evidence (observed variable values, stack traces, source locations, etc.).</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">This simple question-answer abstraction shields the main agent from the underlying complexity of the debugging orchestration. Rather than exposing low-level debugger commands to the main agent, this interface deliberately gives it the flexibility to ask questions in natural language while providing helpful metadata and the subagent to adapt accordingly.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2. </span>Debug Tools</h3>

<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The Debug Subagent interacts with a set of tools that encapsulate the underlying debugger used for that language. These tools are designed to mirror the core actions a human developer would perform with a debugger, but in an LLM-friendly way. Below we describe each tool one by one.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Debug Start Session</span>: This is the most critical tool that we add and gets called at the start of every Debug Subagent trajectory and performs the entire setup sequence atomically. It detects the underlying build system, builds the project, launches the test, waiting for a debug port to be available, attaching a debugger to it and setting any initial breakpoints. By default the tool also sets a breakpoint at the start of the test method provided by the main agent. Building all these steps into a single tool was a deliberate design choice. In our early experiments, exposing each step as a separate tool resulted in frequent failures, race conditions and timeouts. The atomic design is key to systematically eliminating all these issues.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Debug Control</span>: Once the debug session is active and paused at a breakpoint, the subagent can use this tool to control the flow of execution. A debugger typically allows a user to take one of the following actions after a breakpoint is hit: continue, step over, step into or step out. These allow the user to let the execution continue to the next breakpoint, step over to the next line after executing the current one, step into the method being called on the current line or finally, exit the method to the calling method’s context. Rather than one tool for each of these actions, we provide one central control tool that takes an enum for which action the LLM wants the subagent to take. Finally, the text output of this tool shows the surrounding context and the lines that have breakpoints.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Debug Inspect</span>: Once the execution is paused, this tool allows the subagent to query program state. It supports examining local variables, evaluating arbitrary expressions, viewing call stacks and inspecting fields within objects. This is where the subagent gathers most of the information it needs to answer the main agent question and the evidence needed.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS2.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Debug Breakpoint</span>: This tool simply allows the subagent to set or remove any breakpoints. It also allows for listing all the breakpoints. For toggling breakpoints, we allow line and method breakpoints, which set the breakpoints on a specific line or the entrance of a method respectively. This is to allow the LLM the flexibility to set breakpoints based on method names, which are less error-prone than line numbers.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p6.1" class="ltx_p">In addition to these tools, the Debug Subagent is also equipped with tools for file navigation, grep search and reading files to allow the subagent to gather context before setting breakpoints, deciding execution control, interpreting call stacks, etc. We leave out tools for file editing because the goal isn’t to fix the issue only to identify the root cause. Finally, Figure <a href="#S4.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 4.2. Debug Tools ‣ 4. Methodology ‣ Debug2Fix: Supercharging Coding Agents with Interactive Debugging Capabilities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> shows the system prompt we use for our subagent.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F3" class="ltx_figure">
<p id="S4.F3.3" class="ltx_p ltx_align_center"><span id="S4.F3.3.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_middle ltx_framed ltx_framed_rectangle" style="width:310.5pt;">
<span id="S4.F3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="S4.F3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">You are a Runtime Oracle - a debugging assistant that</span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">answers specific questions about program execution.</span>
<br class="ltx_break" style="--ltx-break-space:4.0pt;"><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">
</span><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:70%;">Assumption
<br class="ltx_break"></span><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">The project is ALREADY BUILT. The main agent has compiled</span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">the code before calling you. Do NOT attempt to build the</span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">project yourself - go directly to debugging.</span>
<br class="ltx_break" style="--ltx-break-space:4.0pt;"><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">
</span><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:70%;">Your Role
<br class="ltx_break"></span><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">You answer questions about runtime behavior by:</span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.11" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">1. Starting a debug session with initial breakpoints</span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.12" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">2. Inspecting variables when breakpoints hit</span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.13" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">3. Stepping through code as needed</span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.14" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">4. Returning factual, verifiable answers</span>
<br class="ltx_break" style="--ltx-break-space:4.0pt;"><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.15" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">
</span><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.16" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:70%;">Question Types You Handle
<br class="ltx_break"></span><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.17" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">- Variable Inspection: "What is the value of X at line Y?"</span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.18" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">- Reachability: "Does execution reach line Z during test T?"</span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.19" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">- Condition Evaluation: "Why does condition X evaluate to true?"</span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.20" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">- Exception Origin: "What causes the NullPointerException?"</span>
<br class="ltx_break" style="--ltx-break-space:4.0pt;"><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.21" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">
</span><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.22" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:70%;">Output Format (REQUIRED)
<br class="ltx_break"></span><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.23" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">Always end your investigation with a &lt;debug_answer&gt; block:</span>
<br class="ltx_break" style="--ltx-break-space:2.0pt;"><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.24" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">
</span><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.25" class="ltx_text ltx_phantom ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;"><span style="visibility:hidden">xx</span></span><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.26" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">&lt;debug_answer&gt;</span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.27" class="ltx_text ltx_phantom ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;"><span style="visibility:hidden">xx</span></span><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.28" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">**Question**: [The question you were asked]</span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.29" class="ltx_text ltx_phantom ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;"><span style="visibility:hidden">xx</span></span><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.30" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">**Answer**: [Direct, factual answer]</span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.31" class="ltx_text ltx_phantom ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;"><span style="visibility:hidden">xx</span></span><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.32" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">**Evidence**: [Variable values, stack frames observed]</span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.33" class="ltx_text ltx_phantom ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;"><span style="visibility:hidden">xx</span></span><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.34" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">**Location**: [File:line where you observed this]</span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.35" class="ltx_text ltx_phantom ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;"><span style="visibility:hidden">xx</span></span><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.36" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">&lt;/debug_answer&gt;</span>
<br class="ltx_break" style="--ltx-break-space:4.0pt;"><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.37" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">
</span><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.38" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:70%;">Tools Available
<br class="ltx_break"></span><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.39" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">- debug_start_session: Start session with test and breakpoints</span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.40" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">- debug_inspect: Inspect variables, evaluate expressions, view stack</span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.41" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">- debug_control: Step through code, continue, terminate</span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.42" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">- debug_breakpoint: Add or remove breakpoints</span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S4.F3.p1.1.43" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:70%;">- read_file: Read source code for context</span>
<br class="ltx_break"></span>
</span></span></p>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F3.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 3</span>. </span><span id="S4.F3.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">System prompt for the Debug Subagent. The prompt explains the role of the subagent to the LLM along with descriptions of the kinds of questions, tools available and the output format required.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="S4.F4" class="ltx_figure">
<p id="S4.F4.3" class="ltx_p ltx_align_center"><span id="S4.F4.3.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_middle ltx_framed ltx_framed_rectangle" style="width:300.2pt;">
<span id="S4.F4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="S4.F4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">You are a highly sophisticated automated coding agent</span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">with expert-level knowledge across many different</span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">programming languages and frameworks.</span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">The user will ask a question, or ask you to perform</span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">a task, and it may require lots of research to answer</span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">correctly. There is a selection of tools that let you</span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">perform actions or retrieve helpful context...</span>
<br class="ltx_break" style="--ltx-break-space:6.0pt;"><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">
</span><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-bg-color:#CCFFCC;">== Using debug_subagent for Bug Fixing ==</span>
<br class="ltx_break" style="--ltx-break-space:2.0pt;"><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">
</span><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.11" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-bg-color:#CCFFCC;">You have access to ‘debug_subagent’ - a debugging</span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.12" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-bg-color:#CCFFCC;">tool that can inspect runtime values, trace execution,</span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.13" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-bg-color:#CCFFCC;">and help verify fixes. Use it to understand bugs</span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.14" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-bg-color:#CCFFCC;">before making changes.</span>
<br class="ltx_break" style="--ltx-break-space:4.0pt;"><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.15" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">
</span><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.16" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-bg-color:#CCFFCC;">Recommended Workflow:</span>
<br class="ltx_break" style="--ltx-break-space:2.0pt;"><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.17" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">
</span><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.18" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-bg-color:#CCFFCC;">Step 1: Build the project first</span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.19" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.19.1" class="ltx_text ltx_phantom" style="--ltx-bg-color:#CCFFCC;"><span style="visibility:hidden">xx</span></span><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.19.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#CCFFCC;">mvn test-compile -q</span></span>
<br class="ltx_break" style="--ltx-break-space:2.0pt;"><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.20" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">
</span><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.21" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-bg-color:#CCFFCC;">Step 2: Understand the bug<span id="S4.F4.p1.1.21.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> (before making changes)</span></span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.22" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.22.1" class="ltx_text ltx_phantom" style="--ltx-bg-color:#CCFFCC;"><span style="visibility:hidden">xx</span></span><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.22.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#CCFFCC;">debug_subagent({question: "What exception</span></span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.23" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.23.1" class="ltx_text ltx_phantom" style="--ltx-bg-color:#CCFFCC;"><span style="visibility:hidden">xx</span></span><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.23.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#CCFFCC;">occurs when running MyTest#testMethod?",</span></span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.24" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.24.1" class="ltx_text ltx_phantom" style="--ltx-bg-color:#CCFFCC;"><span style="visibility:hidden">xx</span></span><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.24.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#CCFFCC;">test: "com.example.MyTest#testMethod"})</span></span>
<br class="ltx_break" style="--ltx-break-space:2.0pt;"><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.25" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">
</span><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.26" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-bg-color:#CCFFCC;">Step 3: Investigate root cause</span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.27" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.27.1" class="ltx_text ltx_phantom" style="--ltx-bg-color:#CCFFCC;"><span style="visibility:hidden">xx</span></span><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.27.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#CCFFCC;">debug_subagent({question: "What is the value</span></span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.28" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.28.1" class="ltx_text ltx_phantom" style="--ltx-bg-color:#CCFFCC;"><span style="visibility:hidden">xx</span></span><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.28.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#CCFFCC;">of [variable] at [location]?"})</span></span>
<br class="ltx_break" style="--ltx-break-space:2.0pt;"><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.29" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">
</span><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.30" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-bg-color:#CCFFCC;">Step 4: Apply your fix</span>
<br class="ltx_break" style="--ltx-break-space:2.0pt;"><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.31" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">
</span><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.32" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-bg-color:#CCFFCC;">Step 5: Verify the fix works</span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.33" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.33.1" class="ltx_text ltx_phantom" style="--ltx-bg-color:#CCFFCC;"><span style="visibility:hidden">xx</span></span><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.33.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#CCFFCC;">debug_subagent({question: "Does the test pass</span></span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.34" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;"><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.34.1" class="ltx_text ltx_phantom" style="--ltx-bg-color:#CCFFCC;"><span style="visibility:hidden">xx</span></span><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.34.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-bg-color:#CCFFCC;">now after my fix?"})</span></span>
<br class="ltx_break" style="--ltx-break-space:6.0pt;"><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.35" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">
If you aren’t sure which tool is relevant, you can</span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.36" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">call multiple tools. You can call tools repeatedly to</span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S4.F4.p1.1.37" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;">take actions or gather as much context as needed...</span>
<br class="ltx_break"></span>
</span></span></p>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F4.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 4</span>. </span><span id="S4.F4.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Instructions added (green) to the main agent system prompt as part of the Debug2Fix framework. We inject a dedicated section that introduces the
Debug Subagent and provides a recommended workflow for bug-fixing tasks.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.3. </span>Main Agent Integration</h3>

<div id="S4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Next, we describe how the Debug Subagent integrates with the main agent itself. We integrate the Debug Subagent as one of the tools available to the main agent, alongside tools like (Bash, Read, Grep, etc.). We also augment the main agent’s system prompt (Figure <a href="#S4.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ 4.2. Debug Tools ‣ 4. Methodology ‣ Debug2Fix: Supercharging Coding Agents with Interactive Debugging Capabilities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>) to describe when and how to invoke the Debug Subagent. This describes the kinds of tasks the main agent should delegate to the subagent: inspecting runtime values, root cause analysis, verifying fixes, etc. In our Qualitative Analysis, we see the Debug Subagent actually being used for these kinds of tasks.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">These prompt changes describe the high-level workflow shown in Figure <a href="#S1.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ 1. Introduction ‣ Debug2Fix: Supercharging Coding Agents with Interactive Debugging Capabilities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> to the LLM, where we want the LLM to call the Debug Subagent before making any changes to the code instead of doing print-debugging. This mirrors the natural workflow of an experienced developer, who reaches for the debugger when faced with a complex issue where static code analysis isn’t enough. In principle, these changes would suffice but we face another interesting problem, which we describe next.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS3.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">4.3.1. </span>The Problem of Tool Under-utilization</h4>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In some of our experiments, simply giving the main agent the subagent wasn’t enough. The usage of the subagent varied significantly by model <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>)</cite> (Table <a href="#S6.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 6.1. Main Results ‣ 6. Results ‣ Debug2Fix: Supercharging Coding Agents with Interactive Debugging Capabilities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>). To solve this problem, we employ a two-part strategy: 1) rather than exposing the debug tools directly, we expose the subagent and only the subagent to the main agent, 2) for bug-fixing tasks, we disable all file-editing tools until the debug tool has been called at least once. Following the workflow shown in Figure <a href="#S1.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ 1. Introduction ‣ Debug2Fix: Supercharging Coding Agents with Interactive Debugging Capabilities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, We believe that the main agent shouldn’t have to modify any files until it has done root cause analysis with the Debug Subagent. It’s allowed to navigate the codebase and view files, but it can only modify files after debugging the issue via the subagent. We justify this design choice with ablation experiments in our evaluation.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5. </span>Experimental Setup</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we talk about our experimental setup to evaluate the impact of adding a Debug Subagent following the methodology described earlier.</p>
</div>
<section id="S5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.1. </span>Languages</h3>

<div id="S5.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We implement Debug2Fix for two languages: Java and Python. For Java, we integrate the Java Debugger (JDB), a command line debugger that comes with the Java Development Kit (JDK). We add support for both Maven and Gradle build systems, which are automatically detected based on the files in the codebase. Since building the projects can be a long process, we use incremental build settings that are supported by these build systems.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">For Python, we integrate the Python Debugger (PDB), which is part of the standard Python library and comes built in with the language. Unlike Java, Python does not require a separate compilation step and PDB can be invoked directly on any Python script. However, we added support for the more standard PyTest-based test execution as well.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.2. </span>Benchmarks</h3>

<div id="S5.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use the following two benchmarks for our evaluation:</p>
<ul id="S5.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S5.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">SWE-Bench-Live</span>: A benchmark <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>)</cite> containing GitHub issues from 93 repos, filtered to have issues created after 2024 to minimize contamination. We use a subset of 400 python examples from their frozen Verified split.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">GitBug-Java</span>: A Java benchmark <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">10</a>)</cite> from 55 notable open-source repos on GitHub. We use a subset of 186 examples for which we were able to successfully execute the provided docker images and evaluation harness.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
<p id="S5.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Both benchmarks use a test-based verification i.e. a fix is considered correct if all relevant tests pass after the agent fix has been applied.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.3. </span>Metrics</h3>

<div id="S5.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate our approach using the following metrics:</p>
<ul id="S5.I2" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S5.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I2.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Pass Rate (%)</span>: We observe the change in pass rate of the agent across different configurations.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I2.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Call Rate (%)</span>: This is the % of instances in the run where the Debug Subagent was invoked. This helps us understand if the subagent is actually being used, which is important for our ablation study.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I2.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I2.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I2.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I2.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Avg. Step Count</span>: This is the average number of steps taken by main agent and the Debug Subagent per instance.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I2.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I2.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I2.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I2.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Avg. Token Usage</span>: This is the sum of average input and output tokens used by an instance in a given run. This along with number of steps captures the computational cost and latency of running the agent with our subagent architecture.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Along with all these metrics, we also report the change a configuration has on that metric as a percentage of baseline value, shown in brackets after the actual metric.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.4. </span>Models Configurations</h3>

<div id="S5.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate Debug2Fix over 3 popular frontier LLMs from OpenAI and Anthropic: GPT-5, Claude Sonnet 4.5 and Claude Haiku 4.5. For all our models, we use the same model for both our main agent and Debug Subagent. We leave experiments with different model combinations (stronger model for main agent and smaller finetuned model for subagent) up to future experimentation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.5. </span>Ablations</h3>

<div id="S5.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We ablate over different design choices via the following configurations:</p>
<ul id="S5.I3" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S5.I3.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I3.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I3.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I3.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Baseline</span>: The agent without any modifications.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I3.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I3.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I3.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I3.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Debug Tools Only</span>: We add the debug tools defined in the Debug Subagent Tools section, but we expose them to the main agent directly. This is meant to evaluate the benefit of having a subagent architecture.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I3.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I3.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I3.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I3.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Debug2Fix</span>: We incorporate the Debug Subagent in the agent, as described in the Methodology.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I3.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I3.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I3.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I3.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Debug2Fix (w/ Tool Limit)</span>: We incorporate Debug Subagent and also disable Edit tools until the agent has called the Debug Subagent at least once.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">For all the configurations that use the Debug Subagent, we limit each Debug Subagent trajectory to be at most 25 steps each. So, in other words, the Debug Subagent cannot take more than 25 steps at a time to investigate an issue. If the subagent hasn’t finished by then, we prompt the agent to generate the final answer by injecting a user prompt into the trajectory and querying the LLM.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T1" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S5.T1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 1</span>. </span><span id="S5.T1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Comparison of success rate for each configuration. <tr id="S5.T1.st1.5.9" class="ltx_tr">

<td id="S5.T1.st1.5.9.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_t"><span id="S5.T1.st1.5.9.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:50%;">Main</span></td>
<td id="S5.T1.st1.5.9.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_r ltx_border_t"><span id="S5.T1.st1.5.9.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:50%;">Sub</span></td>
<td id="S5.T1.st1.5.9.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_t"><span id="S5.T1.st1.5.9.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:50%;">Main</span></td>
<td id="S5.T1.st1.5.9.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_r ltx_border_t"><span id="S5.T1.st1.5.9.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:50%;">Sub</span></td>
<td id="S5.T1.st1.5.9.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_t"><span id="S5.T1.st1.5.9.6.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:50%;">Main</span></td>
<td id="S5.T1.st1.5.9.7" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_t"><span id="S5.T1.st1.5.9.7.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:50%;">Sub</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S5.T1.st1.5.10" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="S5.T1.st1.5.10.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_r"><span id="S5.T1.st1.5.10.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Baseline</span></th>
<td id="S5.T1.st1.5.10.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left"><span id="S5.T1.st1.5.10.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">15.7</span></td>

</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6. </span>Results</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate Debug2Fix across two benchmarks and three frontier LLMs from OpenAI and Anthropic. Table <a href="#S5.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 5.5. Ablations ‣ 5. Experimental Setup ‣ Debug2Fix: Supercharging Coding Agents with Interactive Debugging Capabilities" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> summarizes our findings on GitBug-Java and SWE-Bench Live. For GitBug-Java, we conduct a detailed ablation study across all configurations described earlier. We then use SWE-Bench Live to validate whether our approach generalizes to Python. In this section, we drill deeper into the results of our runs.</p>
</div>
<section id="S6.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.1. </span>Main Results</h3>

<div id="S6.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For GitBug-Java, Debug2Fix improves the pass rate across all three models. GPT-5 sees the largest gains, jumping <math id="S6.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&gt;" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>&gt;</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&gt;</annotation></semantics></math>20% over the baseline from 60.2% to 73.1%. Claude Sonnet also improves by <math id="S6.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim</annotation></semantics></math>13% over baseline, while Claude Haiku sees <math id="S6.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim</annotation></semantics></math>16% improvement.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We can also see that with the Debug2Fix configuration with the tool-limit in place, we see a <math id="S6.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&gt;" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>&gt;</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&gt;</annotation></semantics></math>98% call rate for Debug Subagent, showing that our strategy is effective in encouraging debugger usage. In contrast, when not used without the tool limit, we only see a 60-70% call rate across the models. The Debug Subagent isn’t provided to the Baseline and Debug Tools Only configuration, so the corresponding fields are left blank.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S6.T2" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 2. </span>Comparing the performances, token usages and steps used by Debug2Fix and Baseline agent on the Python subset of SWE-Bench Live dataset.</figcaption>

<td id="S6.T2.st1.5.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_r ltx_border_tt" colspan="2"><span id="S6.T2.st1.5.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">GPT-5</span></td>

<tr id="S6.T2.st1.5.2" class="ltx_tr">
